articles.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
articles.summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals

articles.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
articles.summary: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. articles.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
articles.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. articles.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
articles.summary: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. articles.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
articles.summary: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<α<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. articles.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
articles.summary: Deep learning training is difficult to verify within a scientific workflow: its architecture, hyperparameters, and procedure are rarely fixed until training has been attempted, and two honest runs never produce the same weights, so recomputation cannot serve as a check. articles.title: VLT and Keck recovery and characterisation of 2025 SC$_{79}$: linking 'Ayló'chaxnim and Atira asteroids
articles.summary: Asteroids near the boundary between the Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim classes can trace dynamical links between the two populations, but their small solar elongations make recovery and physical characterisation difficult. We recover 2025 SC$_{79}$, measure its optical colours, and investigate its likely source region and transitions between these populations. articles.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
articles.summary: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. articles.title: Unraveling square and kagome lattice frustrated magnetism by scalable tensor networks
articles.summary: We extend the scalability of variational infinite two-dimensional tensor network methods with application to investigate frustrated magnetism of the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model and kagome-lattice Heisenberg model. In the sign-problem-free limit of the square-lattice model, we achieve high ground-state energy precision comparable to quantum Monte Carlo methods. articles.title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
articles.summary: Zeolites are an important class of porous crystalline materials with broad applications in gas storage, separations, and catalysis. Although hundreds of thousands of experimentally realized and hypothetical zeolite structures are known, identifying materials optimized for a target application remains challenging because property labels are expensive to obtain and available only for limited structure-molecule pairs. articles.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
articles.summary: Tendon-driven continuum robots can reach through constrained spaces, but contact along their bodies is invisible to the sensors at their motors. We show that this is a structural limitation rather than a tuning problem: the map from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space of dimension at least seven, so no estimator that leaves the contact support free can locate contact. articles.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
articles.summary: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. articles.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. articles.title: An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection
articles.summary: Regression testing assesses whether software components that have already been developed and tested continue to work correctly after modifications. Ideally, regression testing re-executes the entire test suite after each modification, but this is infeasible in real-world scenarios because of the computational burden; therefore, optimized approaches, such as Test Case Selection, have been developed. articles.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
articles.summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) improve task performance by generating longer intermediate reasoning traces, but this substantially increases inference costs and makes low-precision quantization increasingly important. articles.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
articles.summary: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. articles.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
articles.summary: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge. articles.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. articles.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
articles.summary: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis. articles.title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole
articles.summary: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordström black hole.

articles.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
articles.summary: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. articles.title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
articles.summary: Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. articles.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
articles.summary: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. articles.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
articles.summary: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. articles.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
articles.summary: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. articles.title: The AIDA-TNG project: Galactic bar pattern speeds in self-interacting dark matter
articles.summary: Cosmological simulations within the standard cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm systematically predict higher values of the dimensionless bar-speed parameter, $\boldsymbol{R} \equiv R_{\mathrm{cr}}/R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ (where $R_{\mathrm{cr}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{bar}}$ denote the corotation radius and the bar radius, respectively), than those inferred from observations of local galaxies, a discrepancy known as the fast-bar tension. articles.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
articles.summary: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. articles.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
articles.summary: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1. The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. articles.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
articles.summary: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. articles.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
articles.summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. articles.title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
articles.summary: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. articles.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
articles.summary: Data deduplication has become increasingly important in large-scale storage systems, driven by the rapid growth of digital data. By identifying and removing repeats in the data stream, deduplication saves storage space more efficiently than traditional compression methods. articles.title: GroundWork: Bridging Human and LLM Reasoning Through a Structured Argumentation Model
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into workflows that require reasoning over text documents, yet interaction remains largely conversational. This leaves argumentative structure implicit or embedded in text, making it difficult to maintain, compare, and revise arguments as analyses evolve. articles.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
articles.summary: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. articles.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
articles.summary: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. articles.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
articles.summary: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. articles.title: Ensemble Individual Mode Frequency Modeling of Kepler Giants - Extending the IACgrid towards the red-giant branch
articles.summary: Precise stellar parameters, in particular ages, are vital for understanding the formation and history of the Milky Way. Usually, this is achieved by fitting stellar evolution models to observational constraints such as spectroscopic and astrometric parameters. articles.title: The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs
articles.summary: Investors turn signals into holdings through decision rules: buy the top decile, hold stocks with high momentum and low volatility, exclude stocks that fail a screen. Many such rules are Boolean functions of threshold statements about signal ranks, and writing them this way shows both what a rule holds and how often it trades. articles.title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
articles.summary: Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions.

articles.summary: Non-Gaussian perturbations generated during inflation can often be described perturbatively via integrals of kernels acting on Gaussian fields. In this work, we investigate, in a model-independent manner, whether these kernels can produce parity-violating (PV) contributions to the trispectrum, and which Wick's theorem contraction configurations of the Gaussian fields lead to them. articles.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. articles.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
articles.summary: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. Beyond the initial X-ray burst, electrons released by radioactive fission products can become trapped in Earth's magnetic field, repeatedly exposing satellites as an artificial radiation belt. articles.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry

articles.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
articles.summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. articles.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
articles.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. articles.title: Mellin Transform formulas for special values of Goss $L$-functions
articles.summary: In the present paper, we provide formulas for the special values of dual Goss $L$-functions of Drinfeld modules at any non-negative integer in terms of the determinant of the values of a motivic map, extensively studied by both authors in 2026, for a large class of Anderson modules. Our result may be seen as a function field analogue of conjectural formulas for special values of motivic $L$-functions in terms of algebraic Mellin integrals.

articles.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
articles.summary: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. articles.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
articles.summary: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein representations and as a prior for editing them. articles.title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
articles.summary: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records.
